blogs.title: The Information Predicament: Why *Ciminelli*'s Property Rule Didn't Defeat *Constantinescu*
blogs.description: This post analyzes the Fifth Circuit's navigation of the Supreme Court's *Ciminelli* holding, which barred fraud convictions based solely on the deprivation of 'valuable economic information.' Explore how *Constantinescu* distinguishes the indictment's allegation of 'fraudulent inducement to purchase securities' (protecting a money transaction) from the 'right-to-control' theory rejected in *Ciminelli*, clarifying the specific pleading threshold plaintiffs must meet when charging digital market manipulation that relies on trading data.

blogs.title: Profit Over Loss: How *Kousisis* Redefined Fraudulent Intent in Federal Indictments
blogs.description: Focus on the independent claim that defendants' intent to 'profit' negates a 'intent to defraud' under 18 U.S.C. § 1348. This article details how the Fifth Circuit applied the 2025 *Kousisis* decision to show that a scheme to 'obtain money through false pretenses' satisfies the intent to defraud element without requiring proof that the victim suffered an economic loss. This post examines the implications of this ruling for defense arguments regarding 'clean profit' in securities fraud cases.

blogs.title: Influencers in Flight: *Constantinescu*'s Impact on Digital Pump-and-Dump Prosecutions
blogs.description: Long-term implications for the government and prosecutors charging 'social-media influencers' with fraud. This post analyzes how *Constantinescu*'s adherence to the *Rafoi* sufficiency standard ensures that digital amplification of 'trading positions' is treated as a capital offense in the securities code. It contrasts traditional fraud requirements with the unique risks of algorithmically sustained deception in the age of influencer culture.
